result:
I wrote `tests/test_d10_site.py` with 15 tests. 6 fail on the current code, as expected, and 9 pass. I didn't write or change anything outside `tests/`.

The 6 failures:
- `design.html` still has the Option tag and style, the "Ce qui tient dans vos limites" block and the "Jusqu'à 2,0 %" card.
- It has no headroom line.
- `whatif.py`'s docstring doesn't yet present scenarios as user-chosen.

The `whatif.py` tests that already pass include a real `build()` run. It takes about 4 seconds, offline, with `TARGETS` cut to `(5.0,)`.

- `test_design_text_has_no_advisory_phrase`: the visible design copy contains none of the SPEC §9.3 item 3 blocklist phrases, matched case- and accent-insensitively (D10 item 4).
- `test_design_source_has_no_advisory_phrase_in_attributes`: the same blocklist holds over the whole HTML source, including attributes and comments but not script or style (§9.3 item 3).
- `test_design_has_no_option_or_alternative_wording`: no "option(s)" or "alternative(s)" in the visible text, and no `k-option` or "option" anywhere in the markup or CSS (D10 item 2, SPEC §8).
- `test_design_removed_fits_in_limits_block_and_card`: the "Ce qui tient dans vos limites" block and the "Jusqu'à X %" card are gone, along with the three prorata and ZST.TO variant cards (D10 item 2).
- `test_design_no_text_suggests_a_funding_variant_or_size`: no "prorata", "pro rata" or "Depuis ZST.TO" funding variant appears (D10 item 1).
- `test_design_has_factual_headroom_line_in_flow_b_report`: board 2 contains the FR §8 template, « Avec le financement indiqué (ZST.TO), la transaction franchit votre limite H9 au-delà de X %. ».
- `test_design_headroom_line_is_flow_b_only`: the headroom line is absent from the home board (0) and the flow-A approval board (4) (§9.2, §20.7).
- `test_design_headroom_line_has_no_action_framing`: the headroom line carries no "Jusqu'à", "tient" or similar framing (D10, §8).
- `test_design_does_not_rank_or_prefer_choices`: no "meilleur", "best", "prochaine étape" or "next step" style ranking or preference copy (D10 item 1).
- `test_whatif_strings_and_docstrings_have_no_option_ranking_or_advice`: no best, fits, option, alternative or ranking wording, and no blocklist phrase, in `whatif.py`'s docstrings, string constants or dict keys (D10 items 1, 2 and 4).
- `test_whatif_docstrings_present_scenarios_as_user_chosen`: the module docstring says the user picks the asset, size and funding, says nothing is recommended or ranked, and no longer says "put it at" (D10).
- `test_whatif_does_not_sort_or_rank_by_outcome`: an AST scan finds no sorted, max, min or sort call keyed on verdict, metrics, checks or cone (D10, §8).
- `test_whatif_pure_helpers_emit_no_ranking_or_option_fields`: `_shares`, `_cone` and `_val` run on a tiny input and their outputs contain no forbidden keys (D10 item 2).
- `test_whatif_module_names_have_no_option_or_ranking_vocabulary`: no name defined in `whatif.py` has best, rank, option, alternative, fit, recommend or suggest vocabulary (D10).
- `test_whatif_build_output_schema_and_narrative`: the `whatif.json` and `universe.json` keys contain no forbidden fields. Scenario keys are `size|funding`, ordered by input size, and the universe is ordered by name. Every narrative segment passes the blocklist (D10 items 1, 2 and 4).

I made two stricter-reading calls and marked them `# SPEC-AMBIGUITY:` in the test file:
- "dans vos limites" is banned entirely, because the removed block used that wording to present sizes as acceptable.
- The `whatif.py` docstring wording is only loosely specified, so the test requires it to credit the user with the choice and to say there is no recommendation or ranking.

I also decided the "outside the disclaimer" exclusion is a no-op for now, since `design.html` has no disclaimer text. The test strips the fixed FR disclaimer if one gets added.
